clue.text: What toppled surfer with a heartless violence?

indicators.note: a word with no heart has lost its middle, so only its two ends remain

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
taken as written
only the first and last letters of violence are kept

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what violent force knocked a surfer off the board.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by description: the thing that knocks a surfer over.
explanation.definitionFit: A breaking swell of the sea is precisely what tips a rider off a board into the water.

clue.text: Dissenter caught breaking into various locations

indicators.note: various suggests things scattered in different arrangements, so the following letters are mixed up
breaking into means forcing a way inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A rebel is arrested while burgling a series of different premises.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attacks cherished beliefs or established institutions is a kind of dissenter from orthodoxy.

clue.text: French article unclear, dismissing initial alliance

indicators.note: dismissing the initial means sending away the opening letter of the preceding word

blocks.note: le is a French word for the
something unclear is vague

explanation.surface: A grammar note: a French article is hazy, and something about an initial alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is a formal union of states, clubs or people joined for a common purpose.

clue.text: Limits to some battlefield in concealed state

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its boundaries, its first and last letters

blocks.note: the two edge letters of some
Crecy in northern France was the site of the 1346 battle won by Edward III

explanation.surface: Military restrictions leave parts of a battlefield hidden from view.
explanation.definitionFit: Secrecy is the condition of being kept hidden, a state in which things are not revealed.

clue.text: Too chill at sea? Here's waterproof stuff

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and lost, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Cold sailors are offered a protective material to keep the weather off.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilcloth is cotton fabric treated with oil to make it shed water, used for tablecloths and covers.

clue.text: Closely note taste in music?

blocks.note: N is a common abbreviation for note
having an ear means having a feel for music

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pay careful attention to musical preference.
explanation.walkthrough: Closely is read as the adverb at the front, not as an instruction to the note.
explanation.definitionFit: As adverbs both describe being a short distance away, as in staying near or closely beside someone.

clue.text: Sinister Parisian displaying inelegance

blocks.note: first meaning: sinister in its heraldic sense of left, as the French say it
second meaning: socially awkward and clumsy

explanation.surface: A menacing Frenchman who is also rather clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinister is Latin for left, and the French word for left also means awkward in English.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for left-hand has been borrowed into English to describe tactless, ungraceful behaviour.

clue.text: Disease curtailed sight? Extra writing added to large amount probing that

indicators.note: curtailed means its tail is cut off, so the last letter goes
added to means one piece is placed straight after another
something probing pushes its way inside, so it ends up within the other part

blocks.note: the eye is the organ of sight; that refers back to it
a pile is a large quantity
a postscript adds writing after a letter is signed

explanation.surface: A sequence of medical notes on failing sight and extra text in a big document.
explanation.walkthrough: That points back to the shortened sight, which receives the large amount plus extra writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder causing recurrent seizures, which makes it a medical condition or disease.

clue.text: Author's position over red meat I twice ignored

indicators.note: the letter I is to be left out on two occasions, once from each piece

blocks.note: a site is a position or location
venison, deer meat, is a red meat

explanation.surface: A writer's standpoint is set above his views on eating red meat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, over places the first piece above the second. Each piece loses one I.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island and Kidnapped, so the surname names a celebrated writer.

clue.text: Young person's type of shirt - new snazzy gear

indicators.note: snazzy means flashily stylish, as if dressed up and rearranged

blocks.note: a tee is a T-shirt
N is the standard abbreviation for new
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A young person wearing a T-shirt and some fashionable new clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged from thirteen to nineteen is a youth, a person still growing up.

clue.text: Stays ready after reduction in crop?

indicators.note: a reduction cuts the word down, here by losing its final letter
after places the first word mentioned behind the second one

blocks.note: corn is a cereal crop
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: Harvest remains prepared after a smaller crop yield.
explanation.walkthrough: Stays reads as a verb, but it is the old plural noun for a stiffened bodice.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays is the traditional name for a laced, boned undergarment shaping the torso.

clue.text: Source of water current, cold, that is infiltrated by chlorine

indicators.note: to be infiltrated is to have something slip inside you

blocks.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
C stands for cold on taps
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine

explanation.surface: A chlorinated water supply with a cold flow, described by a pool engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: Water drips from the hanging ice as it melts, so the definition is a little cryptic but fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging spike of ice yields drops when it thaws, making it a frozen reservoir of meltwater.

clue.text: Dish state function involving trace of socialism

indicators.note: a trace is the smallest hint of something, here only its first letter
involving means taking in, so the small piece is held within

blocks.note: case means a condition or state, as in in a bad case
the first letter of socialism
a role is a function someone performs

explanation.surface: A state banquet with a hint of left-wing politics on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A casserole is a stew slowly cooked in the oven, served as a dish in the same pot.

clue.text: Note fork (article not needed for feed)

indicators.note: the article is not needed, so the indefinite article's letter is dropped from the next word

blocks.note: a crotch is a fork, as in a tree or the legs
to feed is to eat

explanation.surface: A note about table manners: use a fork, but nothing else is needed for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The article removed is A, the indefinite article.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a crotchet is a musical note lasting one beat, what Americans call a quarter note.

clue.text: Caught with a sign of discontent about national symbol? Disguise required!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written
a moue is a pout of displeasure
a flag is a nation's emblem

explanation.surface: A protester is arrested grimacing at a flag and urgently needs a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Camouflage is concealment by blending into the surroundings, a form of disguise.

clue.text: Uncommon success in bowling engrosses son

indicators.note: to engross is literally to take in wholly, so the son is absorbed within

blocks.note: in tenpin bowling a spare is knocking all pins down with two balls
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A rare bowling triumph completely absorbs a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sparse is thinly scattered and scarce, so it is uncommon or rare.

clue.text: Wise in restricting a parasite's destructive activity

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the outer word confines the others

blocks.note: a sage is wise
taken as written
a bot is the parasitic larva of the botfly

explanation.surface: Clever control of a pest that does damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate wrecking or obstruction, an act intended to destroy or damage.

clue.text: River quietens after introduction of hydrant

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening, its first letter
the second word is read after something has been put into it

blocks.note: to tame something is to calm and subdue it
the first letter of hydrant

explanation.surface: A river calms once a fire hydrant is installed.
explanation.walkthrough: The hydrant's letter is introduced into the word for quietens.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames is the major river flowing through London to the North Sea.

clue.text: Confusion after jazz fan's given access to house?

indicators.note: after places the first named item behind the next one

blocks.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
a flap is a state of agitated confusion

explanation.surface: A jazz fan is flustered after being let into a house.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the access is for a pet, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hinged door in an outside door lets a pet come and go from the home.

clue.text: Irish broadcaster in brave broadcast, showing some backbone

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
in places the first item inside the next

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
RTE is Ireland's national broadcaster

explanation.surface: An Irish broadcaster shows backbone in a courageous programme.
explanation.walkthrough: Showing some backbone looks like praise for courage, but it is the definition: one piece of a spine.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertebra is one of the bones making up the spinal column, so it is part of the backbone.

clue.text: English colt abandoning fruit suitable for horses

indicators.note: the colt abandoning the fruit means its letter leaves that word

blocks.note: E abbreviates English
a quince is a hard yellow fruit
C is the abbreviation for colt in racing form

explanation.surface: An English colt refuses fruit, which isn't fit for horses anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine means relating to or like horses, so it describes things fit for or belonging to them.

clue.text: Power increasingly picked up, involving university representative

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, read from the bottom upwards
involving means taking in, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power
more and more, increasingly
U abbreviates university

explanation.surface: Political power grows, with a university involved in the rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the European Parliament is elected to represent constituents in Brussels and Strasbourg.

clue.text: Little point embracing upturn if one's excluded county

indicators.note: one is the letter I, and it is to be left out
embracing means wrapping around, so the outer word encloses the other

blocks.note: a dot is a small point
an upturn is a rise

explanation.surface: There's little point welcoming an improvement if you're left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Upturn is a noun meaning increase, not a signal to reverse anything. Dorset is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is an English county, the region on the southern coast known for the Jurassic Coast.

clue.text: First appearance of some kind legal representative

indicators.note: the first appearance of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of some
an ilk is a type or kind

explanation.surface: A lawyer making a debut appearance of a certain sort.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a silk is a King's Counsel, a senior barrister, from the silk gown they wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior barristers in Britain wear silk gowns, so the fabric names such advocates in court.

clue.text: Revolutionary runner making entry in book of member

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the whole assembly is read backwards
making entry means going inside, so the runner sits between the other pieces

blocks.note: B is an abbreviation for book
a miler is an athlete who runs the mile
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rebel athlete enters the record book of the club's members.
explanation.walkthrough: Member here is a body part, not a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a member of the body; a front leg or arm is one particular such member.

clue.text: Post: old woman has one on line?

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman
I is the Roman numeral one
L abbreviates line

explanation.surface: Wondering if an elderly lady has letters waiting online.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, on places the one above the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail and post are the British and American words for letters delivered by the postal service.

clue.text: Disease from vitamin deficiency: everyone returned to tuck into confection of grape

indicators.note: a confection is something mixed and made up, so the letters are blended anew
returned means sent back, read from right to left
tucking into something means going inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Diet advice: deficiency sufferers all return to eat a sweet grape treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellagra is caused by lack of niacin, a B vitamin, producing dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia.

clue.text: Shaman carrying holy bird

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the outer word contains the next

blocks.note: a mage is a magician or wise man
pi is slang for pious, holy

explanation.surface: A shaman holding a sacred bird in a ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie is a black-and-white bird of the crow family, famed for collecting shiny things.
